1: # kohjoh
2: 
3: a native homebrew port of pokemon heartgold and soulsilver for the original 3DS.
4: this is more of a proof-of-concept than a playable game. expect issues.
5: 
6: runs nearly full speed on real old-3DS hardware, bar the intro ho-oh/lugia & busier game areas 
7: 
8: this repository does not contain any unlicensed game data. 
9: for heartgold, you need a file with sha-1 starting with 4fcded0e2713dc03929845de...

13: - How it works: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)
14: - Testing and profiling: [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md), [docs/lotus.md](docs/lotus.md)

21: ## Installation
22: 
23: You need a 3DS with custom firmware (Luma3DS), the Homebrew Launcher, and your own unmodified USA dump of the game (`.nds`). Python 3.10+ is needed on your PC for one step.
24: 
25: 1. Download from the [latest release](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/kohjoh/releases/latest): `kohjoh-gold.3dsx` (HeartGold) and/or `kohjoh-silver.3dsx` (SoulSilver), and `kohjoh-asset-tools.zip`.
26: 2. Copy the `.3dsx` into the `/3ds/` folder on your SD card, keeping its name: `/3ds/kohjoh-gold.3dsx`.
27: 3. Unzip `kohjoh-asset-tools.zip`. On Windows, drag your `.nds` onto `prepare.bat`. Elsewhere run `python prepare.py your-game.nds`. It checks the dump, then writes a `kohjoh-data/` folder (a few seconds; the ROM is only read, and nothing is uploaded). Add `--sd E:\` (your SD card's drive or mount point) to write straight to `3ds/kohjoh/data/` on the card instead.
28: 4. Copy the contents of `kohjoh-data/` (`heartgold.pak` and `heartgold.manifest.json`, or the `soulsilver` pair) into `/3ds/kohjoh/data/` on the SD card. Create the folders if they don't exist.
29: 5. Launch kohjoh from the Homebrew Launcher.
30: 
31: Never share the `.pak` files: they contain your game's data. Saves are kept on the SD card.
32: 
33: The optional CIA is a Luma3DS HOME Menu shortcut; it launches the 3DSX from that exact path and keeps saves on SD. The forwarder requires Luma3DS and has not yet been tested on hardware.

# AGENTS.md

Repository-wide rules for agent sessions working on kohjoh.

## READ THE WIKI 

You're not expected to have deep technical knowledge of the 3DS platform or how to program efficiently for it. This information has been collected for you already. If it isn't already on disk, clone https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot.git. Always refer to coffeepot's CTR section when you're writing code or planning project changes - read the relevant hardware, firrmware or engineering articles, so you understand what you're working with. If you can't justify a change with real-hardware evidence or a citation from the wiki, you probably should not do it. Never edit coffeepot yourself. If you notice something genuinely incorrect, PR and tell the user. Always follow the wiki's C style guide.

The coffeepot wiki is provided locally on this machine in workdir/coffeepot/.
## Delegating to subagents

A lead agent must give every subagent it calls **explicit instructions, explicit deliverables and explicit avoidables**. This is not optional, and it matters most for implementer agents: they edit files and cannot rely on chat context the lead has not written down.

Every subagent brief must state, in the prompt itself:

1. **Objective** — the one bounded slice to complete, and why it exists.
2. **Allowed paths** — the exact files or directories the subagent may read and edit.
3. **Deliverables** — the concrete output: code, patch files, tests, docs, and the required report format (files changed, commands run, results, open questions).
4. **Acceptance checks** — the commands or observations that prove the work is done, and the expected result.
5. **Avoidables** — what not to touch or do: paths outside the slice, unrelated refactors, the decomp checkout in place, commits/pushes unless explicitly assigned, and any known traps from `kohjoh.md` or `docs/troubleshooting.md`.
6. **Stopping point** — when to stop and report instead of guessing, for example if the slice grows, the brief conflicts with `kohjoh.md`, or an acceptance check cannot pass.

Do not send a subagent a vague goal and let it infer scope. If the lead cannot fill in all six items, the slice is not ready to delegate. A brief that is broader, vaguer or in conflict with `kohjoh.md` should be revised before the call, not discovered by the subagent mid-edit.

Implementer subagents hold `docs/status.md`, `docs/lessons.md` and `kohjoh.md` as required reading; the brief adds the slice-specific detail those files cannot contain. When this file disagrees with an agent definition under `.opencode/agents/` or `.claude/agents/`, this file wins.

## Git identity

The only git identity an agent may use in this repository is:

```text
terezi <jules@foxtails.me>
```

Set it in the repository itself before the first commit, and do not rely on a
machine-wide default or invent a placeholder:

```sh
git config user.name terezi
git config user.email jules@foxtails.me
```

Every agent commit carries both fields. Do not use `A4`,
`a4@example.invalid`, the host's auto-detected address, or any other
identity, and do not author on someone else's behalf. If a commit already
exists under another identity, report it to the lead rather than rewriting
history: an artifact's `build-info` names the commit it was built from, and
re-authoring a commit changes that name.

1: # How kohjoh works
2: 
3: kohjoh runs the original HeartGold/SoulSilver code (the pinned decompilation)
4: on the 3DS with a new runtime and GPU renderer. Imported code is listed in
5: [`PROVENANCE.md`](../PROVENANCE.md); the design brief is [`kohjoh.md`](../kohjoh.md).
6: 
7: ## Two halves, one bridge
8: 
9: | Half | Compiled with | Contents |
10: | --- | --- | --- |
11: | DS side | NitroSDK headers, 4-byte enums | game, Nitro compat ([`src/compat`](../src/compat)), [`src/runtime`](../src/runtime) |
12: | 3DS side | libctru/citro3d, short enums | [`src/app`](../src/app), [`graphics`](../src/graphics), [`audio`](../src/audio), [`storage`](../src/storage), [`diagnostics`](../src/diagnostics) |
13: 
14: They meet only in [`kj_bridge.h`](../src/runtime/kj_bridge.h): fixed-width
15: types, no enums, `kj_ds_*` / `kj_ctr_*` functions.
16: 
17: ## Frame flow
18: 
19: 1. The game's own main loop runs on the main thread (`kj_game_main`).
20: 2. Each DS V-blank wait (`OS_Halt`) calls `kj_ctr_vblank`: APT, input, then a
21:    wait locked to the physical V-blank count. A late frame does not wait, so
22:    the game never loses DS time against the real-time audio; a stall over 30
23:    V-blanks resyncs instead ([`main.c`](../src/app/main.c)).
24: 3. After the V-blank callback and vwait tasks (game patch 2001),
25:    [`kj_frame.c`](../src/runtime/kj_frame.c) runs the H-blank walk and
26:    publishes one coherent snapshot: registers, palettes, OAM, VRAM banks,
27:    per-line registers and the last swapped 3D scene. Loops that never reach
28:    the hook (boot, error screens) publish from the V-blank once more than 4
29:    V-blanks pass without one.
30: 4. [`renderer.c`](../src/graphics/renderer.c) waits for the previous GPU frame
31:    (`C3D_FrameBegin(0)`), records both screens and submits. Nothing reads DS
32:    memory after it returns. If the game is ≥2 refreshes behind, the
33:    presentation (not the game tick) is skipped and counted.
34: 
35: ## 2D ([`g2d.c`](../src/graphics/g2d/g2d.c))
36: 
37: - DS tiles are palette-expanded into a 1024×1024 RGBA5551 atlas
38:   ([`atlas.c`](../src/graphics/resources/atlas.c)), one DS tile per PICA 8×8
39:   tile. A slot is reused only if its tile bytes are byte-identical and its
40:   palette version unchanged: no write tracking, no hashing.
41: - Layers draw in DS priority order, with the 3D scene at BG0's slot. Stencil
42:   bits carry blend-target membership (alpha blend = two draws) and window
43:   regions; BLDY and master brightness are full-screen passes.
44: - Text BG and OBJ layers are retained when their inputs (registers, palette,
45:   map/OAM, ext palettes, the character bytes read) are byte-identical; an
46:   unchanged screen is not drawn or transferred at all.
47: - Frames with per-line register changes are drawn as spans of identical lines.
48: - Top screen: DS 256×192 at 1.25× centred in 400×240; 2D is scissored to the
49:   centre, 3D fills the width. Bottom: 1.25× to 320×240.
50: 
51: ## 3D ([`kj_g3.c`](../src/runtime/kj_g3.c), [`g3d.c`](../src/graphics/g3d/g3d.c))
52: 
53: - The DS side interprets matrix stacks (20.12 fixed), texgen and readable
54:   box/position/vector tests on the CPU. NORMAL latches its transformed normal
55:   and immutable lighting inputs; the PICA evaluates DS diffuse/specular,
56:   shininess, ambient and emission with exact fixed-point rounding.
57: - Lit display lists cache expanded object-space positions and retain live
58:   state events. Source validation is exact; animated matrices and lights do
59:   not prevent reuse. Literal-colour meshes retain the baked block cache.
60: - Vertices stay in object space; each batch carries a palette of up to 16 clip
61:   matrices. The 3DS side multiplies each by one fixup matrix (viewport,
62:   widescreen x-scale 0.8, screen rotation, depth range) and the vertex shader
63:   transforms on the GPU. Lit draws use six clip matrices to leave uniform
64:   space for four lights and the shininess table; the vertex ABI stays 16 bytes.
65: - The prior publish selects capture before the next scene starts. Field and
66:   title producers skip discarded geometry traversal and FIFO submission,
67:   preserving game updates, animation and resource retirement. Other producers
68:   retain the state-preserving decoder fallback.
69: - The box test is widened for widescreen so side content is not culled.
70: - DS textures convert once per content change ([`textures.c`](../src/graphics/g3d/textures.c)).
71: - Not yet supported (counted, never silently dropped): fog, toon/highlight,
72:   edge marking, shadow volumes, wireframe, display capture, bitmap BGs.
73: 
74: ## Audio, storage, diagnostics
75: 
76: - The vendored ARM7 sequencer and DS sound chip mix 32768 Hz stereo on an
77:   audio thread (core 0, above the game) fed by NDSP ([`audio.c`](../src/audio/audio.c)).
78: - Saves: interim raw 512 KiB file; two-generation SaveStore on `wip/savestore`.
79: - Logs go to a memory ring flushed by a low-priority thread; `[perf]`, `[pace]`,
80:   `[gpu]` and `[ds]` aggregates every 600 publishes ([testing](testing.md)).

1: # Lessons
2: 
3: The story of kohjoh so far: what we built, what we learned, what worked, what
4: broke and how we recovered. Last revised 2026-11-16. Current state lives in
5: [status.md](status.md); per-session detail lives in [worklog/](worklog/). The
6: rules that came out of all this are at the end.
7: 
8: ## 1. What we have done
9: 
10: kohjoh is a new HGSS 3DS port: a GPU-native runtime on top of the compile
11: layer vendored from hgss-3ds. The work so far, in order:
12: 
13: 1. **Day one (2026-11-12).** Vendored hgss-3ds's patch stack and build driver
14:    (the decomp compiled under GCC, ~90 verified fixes), wrote the runtime and
15:    renderer, and had Goldenrod rendering in Azahar from a prior bench save.
16:    Found and fixed the PICA tile row-order bug; added frame stepping, state
17:    dumps and an offline DS reference renderer.
18: 2. **Correctness (11-12 to 11-13).** Title-screen Ho-Oh: DS W-buffer depth,
19:    direct G3 command-register writes routed to the geometry engine (patch
20:    0302/2004), a crash handler, an offline projector and a zero-matrix trace.
21:    A complete Windows build guide.
22: 3. **O3DS performance, sessions 2 and 3 (11-13 to 11-14).** Read the first
23:    hardware logs, capped present skipping, shrank the G3 decode loop under the
24:    I-cache, made Pokémon crypto word-wide (game patch 2006), batched geometry
25:    DMA, fixed the display-list cache and made it default, found the sound
26:    mixer thread was never profiled, and added a scene-level profiler.
27: 4. **Audio, session 4 (11-15).** chatlog11's software audio plan in five
28:    passes ([worklog](worklog/2026-11-15-audio.md)): measurement, ordinary-
29:    routing fast path, ADPCM decoded as a run then resampled, exact `div127`,
30:    PKHBT output, 192-frame blocks, held samples by default, a decoded-ADPCM
31:    cache with a verify build, and kernel cache flush for wave buffers.
32:    Azahar Goldenrod mixer 107.6 → 48-49 ticks per channel-sample (14.8% →
33:    5-7% of the core), every step bit-exact. New tests: `sound_arm.py`
34:    (Unicorn full-chip differential), `div127_test.c`, `sndprof.py`.
35: 5. **Geometry PR stack #6/#7/#8 (11-15).** Cheaper FIFO cache-hit keys,
36:    skipping discarded field/title scene production, DS lighting moved to the
37:    PICA with cached expanded lit geometry. Merged into `main` with origin/main;
38:    integration testing found a cache hang (`037e134`) before the push.
39: 6. **Hardware cuts (11-15 to 11-16).** Baked stable lit lists, culled retained
40:    blocks outside the picture, restored the NNS GLB state list from a prefix
41:    snapshot, and skipped disabled lights. Azahar Goldenrod logic 25.35 →
42:    13.38 ms, triangles 5.02M → 1.94M per 600 pictures, with pixel-identical
43:    held frames. Still **O3DS_UNTESTED** on hardware.
44: 7. **Tooling and release.** Junction targets compared through `cygpath`, a
45:    serial variant builder, GitHub Actions edition builds, edition asset
46:    preparation, CIA forwarders, `prepare.py`/`prepare.bat` one-step ROM prep,
47:    a README install walkthrough, and a null-BTP guard (patch 0307, issue #9).
48: 
49: ## 2. What worked
50: 
51: **Strategy**
52: - **Reuse the game-compile layer, rewrite the slow parts.** Vendoring the
53:   hgss-3ds patch stack (with provenance) gave a linking game in hours; the
54:   time went to the runtime and renderer, where hgss-3ds had lost its speed.
55: - **One thread, one publish point.** Rendering at a single coherent point in
56:   the game loop (patch 2001) removed the drawer/game races hgss-3ds spent
57:   weeks on. No locks, no torn frames.
58: - **GPU transform with a matrix palette.** DS matrix, lighting and test
59:   semantics stay on the CPU; object-space vertices go to the PICA. 3D worked
60:   first try, widescreen included (one fixup matrix).
61: - **Doing less instead of doing it faster.** Baking stable lit lists, culling
62:   offscreen retained blocks and restoring the GLB prefix removed work outright
63:   and beat every micro-optimization.
64: - **Read the docs first.** The coffeepot wiki already held "never skip two
65:   pictures in a row" (frame-pacing) and the 16 KiB I-cache cliff
66:   (cpu-optimization, icachebench).
67: 
68: **Finding the truth**
69: - **An independent oracle.** The GBATEK reference renderer found the tile
70:   row-order bug in one comparison after guessing had failed.
71: - **Read the hardware log before the code.** o3ds-log-0's `[pace]` and
72:   `[frame]` lines showed presentation starvation; the per-opcode G3 profile
73:   (probe cost of ~440 ticks, the empty END opcode, subtracted) ranked the
74:   decoder's real costs.
75: - **Real profiling.** Azahar's GDB stub plus a 150-line PC sampler found the
76:   true hotspots, including Pokémon crypto, which no reasoning predicted. A
77:   Unicorn per-address count mapped with `addr2line` later found register
78:   spills stage timers could only hint at.
79: - **Calibrating the emulator.** A 4-instruction loop showed Azahar charges one
80:   tick per instruction: its times are instruction counts, not O3DS time, and
81:   it models neither caches nor PMU.
82: - **Count before you build.** `[sndadpcm]` showed >95% of ADPCM decoding
83:   repeats the same 15-20 sounds and sized the cache arena (256 KiB thrashed).
84:   `[sndlock]` and `[sndout]` showed the game never waited on the sound lock
85:   and the "1 underrun" in every hardware log was start-up, which removed two
86:   planned changes.
87: - **Verify modes.** `KJ_DL_VERIFY` (decode live, compare with replay) found
88:   the display-list bug in one run, and, as a bisector, showed an image diff
89:   did not come from the snapshot restore.
90: 
91: **Keeping changes safe**
92: - **Exact rewrites, checked by counters.** Every decoder change kept the same
93:   batches, draws and triangles per 600 frames.
94: - **A differential harness first.** `sound_arm.py` ran reference and working
95:   mixers on identical random register programs, so every later change was
96:   checked bit for bit in a minute.
97: - **Mutation before trust.** Each new cache got a host test, then the test was
98:   broken on purpose (dropped invalidations, a wrong plane) until it failed.
99:   This exposed weak test designs before they could pass bad code.
100: - **Commit each verified pass.** Every regression stayed bisectable to one
101:   change.
102: - **Test the merged tree before pushing.** The full native suite on the merge
103:   found a hang no single branch showed.
104: 
105: ## 3. What went wrong, and how we recovered
106: 
107: ### Process
108: 
109: | Problem | Recovery / rule |
110: | --- | --- |
111: | **Committing late.** Verified improvements sat uncommitted while riskier work piled on top. | Commit every verified step; gate risky features behind `--define` switches. |
112: | **Building before measuring.** The display-list cache was written before its hit rate was known; most lists straddled DMA bursts or varied per frame. | Measure the opportunity first. |
113: | **Measuring the wrong thing.** The cache replayed 4% of words; the first guess (lists left with BEGIN open) explained 13%. A coverage counter (`[dlcov]`) showed 65% were split mid-command by NitroSDK's 118-word DMA bursts. | Count where the work goes before fixing a guessed cause. |
114: | **Guessing at render state.** Four Ho-Oh experiments (cull, depth, alpha test, blend) changed nothing. Dumping the scene and projecting it on the CPU (`g3_reference.py`) showed 41 all-zero clip matrices per frame: the geometry was wrong, not the GPU path. | Split the pipeline at a dump before toggling GPU state. |
115: | **"Ported" is not "complete".** Patch 0302 converted GXFIFO stores but not the direct command-register stores beside them; the writes vanished silently. | When a hardware access class is ported, scan the whole tree for it (game patch 2004). |
116: | **Misreading a counter.** `[ds] per frame` divides by presented frames; with skips it overstated per-game-frame costs, and a note wrongly claimed "near full speed". | Fixed the docs; counter semantics are written in testing.md. |
117: | **Azahar hid a regression.** PR #8 doubled the O3DS captured frame (36 → 57 ms) while Azahar still showed 30 FPS. | Compare work counts (instructions, triangles, draws, shader instructions per vertex), never Azahar FPS. |
118: | **An unprofiled thread.** The DS sound mixer took 20-30% of the O3DS app core, but Azahar lacked DSP firmware, so `ndspInit` failed and the mixer never ran under test. | Every thread the device runs must run under test (`dspfirm.cdc` is now in Azahar's sdmc). |
119: 
120: ### Performance traps
121: 
122: - **Timing probes that dominate.** Per-call `svcGetSystemTick` pairs cost ~390
123:   ticks and nested DMA callbacks inflated the timed region. Prefer sampling.
124: - **"Uninstrumented" builds still carried probes.** `PORT_NOW` in the H-blank
125:   walk ignored `HGSS_PROFILE_OFF` (~800 tick calls a frame). Probes are now
126:   opt-in (`HGSS_PROFILE=on`).
127: - **Sampler bias.** Tight loops (the crypto XOR) looked bigger in samples than
128:   in `[perf]` time. Cross-check with stage times.
129: - **An uncapped present skip starves the screen.** "Skip when two refreshes
130:   behind" never presents while the game runs slightly over budget: O3DS
131:   Goldenrod ran at half speed but skipped 1606 of 2206 pictures. Skip at most
132:   one picture in a row.
133: - **Azahar cannot see code size.** Force-inlining the vertex fast path made
134:   the decode loop 14.6 KiB against a 16 KiB I-cache (CPI hits 5.6 past
135:   32 KiB). Check hot-function sizes with `nm -S`.
136: - **Bump arenas that flush.** Re-recording into fresh space filled the arena
137:   and flushed it twice per 600 frames (29.6 ms spikes). Reuse an entry's
138:   storage when it re-records.
139: - **Snapshot what repeats, not what nearly repeats.** A full GLB snapshot never
140:   hit because its last word changes per model; splitting at the last command
141:   word made the rest a constant prefix.
142: - **Synthetic workloads mislead caches.** The first audio bench's instruments
143:   were too large to repeat and showed the cache as a loss. Size synthetic data
144:   from logs of the real workload.
145: - **PICA bool uniforms read as false in Azahar** though the shbin, libctru and
146:   citro3d looked correct. Unused `.w` components of float uniforms plus
147:   `cmp`/`jmpc` work. The lit shader has no float uniform space left for new
148:   arrays (91 + 7 of 96).
149: 
150: ### Code bugs
151: 
152: - **Struct layout.** `memset(&s, 0, offsetof(s, array))` left counters after
153:   the array unreset. Reset fields explicitly.
154: - **State valid only after a reset.** The ADPCM cache's bucket table used -1
155:   for empty, set by the reset; `sound_diff.c` skips the reset and hung in
156:   `cache_find`. Links are now index + 1, so the zeroed table is empty. Make
157:   the zeroed state valid.
158: - **A cache check in the wrong path.** An early header comparison in the fill
159:   path compared the wrong bytes. The verify build and harness caught it; every
160:   check belongs where the entry is used.
161: - **A digest that hashed raw addresses** reported a block-size change as a
162:   behaviour change. Hash addresses relative to their buffer.
163: - **A harness `memset` compiled into a call to itself** (GCC loop-pattern
164:   distribution), a hang that looked like a slow emulator. Freestanding
165:   helpers need `no-tree-loop-distribute-patterns`.
166: - **Gaps found only by mutation.** The first coverage programs never shared a
167:   sound between channels or rewrote bytes inside a playing sound, so breaking
168:   cache invalidation still passed. Mutate each safety check once and confirm
169:   the harness fails.
170: 
171: ### Build and environment
172: 
173: - **An unverified build-system change regressed saves.** Switching the SDK shim
174:   from copies to junctions changed what compiled; only a save check caught it.
175: - **A path compare ignored MSYS2's mount spellings.** `Path.resolve()` spells
176:   one directory `/c/...` or `/home/<user>/...` depending on which side of a
177:   junction it starts from, so `link_points_to()` called a correct junction
178:   missing and `_link()` re-ran `mklink /J`. Four parallel variants made three
179:   lose the race. Compare through `cygpath -w` and serialize the variants
180:   (`tools/game/build_variants.py`).
181: - **A shared `build/upstream` checkout carries branch state.** It held
182:   `wip/savestore`'s SDK patch 2003 while building `master`; `check_patches.py`
183:   only detects missing patches, not extra ones. Re-created with
184:   `bootstrap.py --clean` (2026-11-12); do the same after switching branches.
185: - **Stacked PRs (#6 ← #7 ← #8)** target each other's branches; merging into
186:   `main` by push does not close them on GitHub. A PR that adds a game patch
187:   also needs `git -C build/upstream am` before it builds.
188: - **Two harnesses for one module.** `sound_arm.py` resets the chip;
189:   `check_hotpaths.py`'s `sound_diff.c` does not. Run both after mixer changes.
190: 
191: ### Test discipline
192: 
193: - **Contaminated tests.** Live input reached scripted runs. Tests own their
194:   input.
195: - **Harness races.** A second `run.ps1` killed the first's emulator (three
196:   lost runs). Stop the old harness first; one Azahar harness at a time.
197: - **Lost samples.** gdbprof printed nothing when Azahar closed; it now prints
198:   what it has.
199: - **Stale reference images.** A wandering NPC moves with the emulated clock, so
200:   an unchanged binary stopped matching references captured hours earlier;
201:   three bisection builds chased it. Rerun the baseline binary first when only
202:   character positions differ.
203: - **Killing a test that was working.** A host check looked idle (Python at
204:   1.7 s CPU, no children) but its binary ran under another parent. List every
205:   process created since the start, with CPU time, before calling it hung.
206: - **Cygwin signals in a tight loop.** An `alarm()` watchdog never fired; a
207:   watchdog thread with `-finstrument-functions` named the looping function in
208:   one run.
209: 
210: ### Shell and editing hazards
211: 
212: - **Fragile command lines.** Multi-line heredocs with nested quotes were
213:   mangled by the shell wrapper; complex edits belong in script files.
214: - **Escapes through Git Bash.** A `sed` insertion turned a backslash-n in
215:   `hgss_game.py` into a real newline (SyntaxError at build time) and
216:   happened twice more. Use the editor tool, or avoid the escape (`putc(10)`).
217: - **Windows Python turned LF into CRLF** (a 900-line diff). Write with
218:   `newline=''`.
219: - **A stray `cat >` with no input** stalled a command for a minute and left its
220:   scripts unwritten.
221: 
222: ## 4. Themes
223: 
224: 1. **Measure, then change.** Nearly every wasted effort (cache before hit rate,
225:    render-state toggles, sampler or counter misreads) was a guess that a
226:    counter, dump or oracle would have settled in one step.
227: 2. **The emulator is not the device.** Azahar counts instructions. It hides
228:    cache cliffs, PICA cost, missing threads and real timing, so it ranks
229:    instruction-count changes and nothing else.
230: 3. **Trust nothing you have not tried to break.** Verify modes, differential
231:    harnesses and mutation testing caught more bugs than review did.
232: 4. **Small verified commits.** They made bisection cheap and risk containable.
233: 5. **Remove work first, speed it up second.**
234: 
235: ## Rules
236: 
237: 1. Commit each verified step; keep `master` building and verified.
238: 2. Check the Coffeepot wiki and `docs/engineering/hgss-remaster/` before
239:    inventing a technique; cite it.
240: 3. Compare against the oracle or a known-good capture before blaming a subsystem.
241: 4. Profile with PC sampling; treat Azahar time as instruction count.
242: 5. Every cache needs an exact validity check and a verify mode.
243: 6. After any build-system change, rerun intro, Goldenrod (with save) and input.
244: 7. After touching a hot loop, check its size with `nm -S` (16 KiB I-cache).
245: 8. One Azahar harness at a time.
246: 9. After touching the sound mixer, run `tests/native/sound_arm.py`
247:    (bit-exact against `HEAD`) and `tests/native/check_hotpaths.py` before
248:    building.
249: 10. Make zeroed state valid, and mutate each safety check once to confirm its
250:     test fails.
251: 11. After switching branches, run `bootstrap.py --clean`.

1: {"body":"## What

`draw_pass` sends `C3D_CullFace`, `C3D_DepthTest` and `C3D_AlphaBlend` on every batch, and `upload_lighting` re-sends all 32 shininess words whenever the specular table is in use. In a DS scene most consecutive batches repeat that state, and citro3d charges for each of them at draw time.

The cost figures coffeepot cites are the reason this is worth doing (`coffeepot/ctr/engineering/PICA200/gpu-rendering.md`, "What a draw call costs"): a separate draw is ~9.7 us of CPU on an Old 3DS, and *each state change on top is 1-2 us, a tenth of the draw itself* ΓÇö a redundant texture bind costs as much as a real one.

## Measured (sinjoh, Pokemon Platinum field)

Same source, same windowed LOTUS session, standing in Snowpoint City, 600-picture windows at pictures 4201-4800, three consecutive windows per build:

| stage | p50 before | p50 after |
|---|---|---|
| g3d (draw_pass) | 972 us | 832 us |
| publish (g2d+g3d+submit) | 2015 us | 1876 us |

- 15,520 -> 15,560 3D draws / 600 frames (unchanged: this is purely skipped state, no batch is joined)
- 389 program switches, 10,503 palette uploads (12,059 matrices), 9,336 lighting uploads per 600 frames
- `state skips 38,511` per 600 frames, i.e. 63.9 per frame against 78 possible `C3D_*` setter calls (26 draws x 3): **82% of the cull/depth/blend calls were redundant**
- `shininess uploads 0` in this scene: Platinum's field never uses the specular table, so that part is free here, but it is still wasteful to send 32 uniforms whenever a lighting context that does use it changes
- captures at both ends of the window are pixel-identical (`ImageChops.difference` bbox `None` on both screens)

static uint32_t s_last_cull, s_last_depth, s_last_blend;
static uint32_t s_last_shininess[32];
static bool s_shininess_valid;
```

1: {"body":"## The failure mode

A measurement run reported a field split that no source tree could produce: the whole field update 2408 us, its two children absent, three sibling slots `0 us`, all next to 15,520 3D draws. The cause was two builds running against the same object trees at once: the linked binary took `kj_frame.o` from a build that wrote 6 probe slots and `renderer.o` from one that read 11, and they disagree about `kj_ds_profile`'s layout. Nothing failed; the numbers just became fiction.

The same class of bug exists without probes: any edit to a struct in a shared header between two concurrent builds can link a binary whose halves were compiled against different layouts, and it will usually still boot.

## Proposal: make the build refuse to run twice

A lock file next to the build trees, taken at startup and released at exit, plus a check that the recorded PID is still alive so a crashed build does not block forever:

```powershell
# tools/build.ps1
$lock = Join-Path $repo 'build/.build.lock'
if (Test-Path $lock) {
    $pid = (Get-Content $lock -First 1) -as [int]
    if ($pid -and (Get-Process -Id $pid -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        throw "a build is already running (pid $pid); wait for it or remove $lock"
    }
    Remove-Item $lock   # stale
}
Set-Content $lock $PID
try { ...existing build... } finally { Remove-Item $lock -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
```

1: {"body":"## The number worth attacking

On sinjoh's Platinum field (standing, 600-frame windows) the scene submits **26 3D draws per frame for ~568 triangles** ΓÇö about 22 triangles and 20 indices per draw. At the ~9.7 us per separate draw that coffeepot measured on an Old 3DS (`coffeepot/ctr/engineering/PICA200/gpu-rendering.md`, "What a draw call costs"), that is roughly **250 us of CPU per frame** for 26 draws that carry almost no geometry. It is the largest single recoverable block left on the port side of the frame after the state filter in #10.

## Why the obvious fix does nothing

I implemented "join contiguous batches with identical state into one `C3D_DrawElements`" and measured it: **0 joins in the field** and 0 in the title scene.

```
merge joined 0 (blocked state 15093 matrices 0)
```

The block is the *material*, not the matrix palette: every consecutive batch differs in `poly_attr`/`tex_param`/`tex_pltt`. A DS batch is a material with its own palette slice, not a strip of one material ΓÇö that is the structural reason the draw count is high.

## What would actually cut it

Two changes together, in this order:

1. **A union palette per draw.** A batch's matrices are a slice of the frame's matrix array (`first_matrix`/`matrix_count`, `KJ_G3_PALETTE` slots). Several batches that share a state but not a matrix set could share one draw if the vertex shader were given the union of their matrices and their indices were remapped to the union's slots. That needs a per-frame rewritten index buffer (or a per-batch palette index patch), not a `memcmp`.

2. **Grouping by state, not by storage order.** Once the palette is a union, batches become joinable only if they are *sorted* by material. For the opaque pass with depth testing that is safe (the DS's own order only matters for equal-depth ties and for translucent geometry, which stays in its own pass). Translucent batches must keep their order.

## Summary

Kohjoh crashes on **real 3DS hardware** while progressing through the **Whirl Islands Lugia-related story sequence**, around the interaction/event involving the special item or bell associated with Lugia. The system displays Luma/ErrDisp's exception screen and requires a reboot.

**Impact:** Potentially story-blocking; the Lugia encounter/sequence cannot be completed if this reproduces.

## Steps to reproduce (initial report)

1. Load a save with access to the Whirl Islands Lugia story sequence.
2. Enter Whirl Islands and progress to the area/event associated with the Lugia-related special item/bell.
3. Continue the event near the location shown in the reporter's photo (waterfall, ladder and several character sprites).
4. Observe the crash.

**Reproducibility:** Observed once; needs confirmation. The exact interaction/script step and whether the item is Silver Wing, Tidal Bell, or another trigger have **not yet been established**.

## Expected

The Whirl Islands event continues normally, with the relevant dialogue, animation and Lugia encounter.

## Actual

The application aborts to the ErrDisp exception screen instead of continuing. This is a crash of `3dsx_app`, not evidence that the 3DS firmware itself crashed.

### Hardware exception details (transcribed from the photo)

```text
Error type:      exception (data abort)
Process ID:      48
Process name:    3dsx_app
Process title ID: 000400000d710200
PC:              0x00560A90
LR:              0x5F676C64
SP:              0x080FFB40
FAR:             0x00000000
FSR:             0x00000005
R0:              0x00000000
```

The zero fault address suggests an invalid/null-address access; confirm against the faulting instruction before attributing a cause. The unusual LR merits inspection for possible state corruption, but is not proof of it.

## Investigation checklist

- [ ] Reproduce with a save immediately before the Whirl Islands/Lugia event; record exact game version, Kohjoh commit/build, and hardware model.
- [ ] Symbolicate `PC=0x00560A90` against the **matching unstripped ELF/map**; inspect the faulting instruction and call path.
- [ ] Determine whether the crash happens on script transition, object/animation spawn, graphics/resource upload, audio cue, or the actual Lugia encounter.
- [ ] Add bounded logging around event-script execution and resource allocations/loads for this scene; capture the last completed operation.
- [ ] Check whether the corresponding event works in the original DS game, and whether it differs between HeartGold and SoulSilver.
- [ ] Verify any fix on actual 3DS hardware and test replay/return to the area to detect regressions.

## Additional details needed

- Exact save/ROM variant (HeartGold or SoulSilver)
- Kohjoh build or commit
- Whether the error repeats from the same save and the exact dialogue/action preceding it
- Save file and full crash dump / log, if available

3: `draw_pass` sends `C3D_CullFace`, `C3D_DepthTest` and `C3D_AlphaBlend` on every batch, and `upload_lighting` re-sends all 32 shininess words whenever the specular table is in use. In a DS scene most consecutive batches repeat that state, and citro3d charges for each of them at draw time.
4: 
5: The cost figures coffeepot cites are the reason this is worth doing (`coffeepot/ctr/engineering/PICA200/gpu-rendering.md`, "What a draw call costs"): a separate draw is ~9.7 us of CPU on an Old 3DS, and *each state change on top is 1-2 us, a tenth of the draw itself* ΓÇö a redundant texture bind costs as much as a real one.
6: 
7: ## Measured (sinjoh, Pokemon Platinum field)
8: 
9: Same source, same windowed LOTUS session, standing in Snowpoint City, 600-picture windows at pictures 4201-4800, three consecutive windows per build:
10: 
11: | stage | p50 before | p50 after |
12: |---|---|---|
13: | g3d (draw_pass) | 972 us | 832 us |
14: | publish (g2d+g3d+submit) | 2015 us | 1876 us |
15: 
16: - 15,520 -> 15,560 3D draws / 600 frames (unchanged: this is purely skipped state, no batch is joined)
17: - 389 program switches, 10,503 palette uploads (12,059 matrices), 9,336 lighting uploads per 600 frames
18: - `state skips 38,511` per 600 frames, i.e. 63.9 per frame against 78 possible `C3D_*` setter calls (26 draws x 3): **82% of the cull/depth/blend calls were redundant**
19: - `shininess uploads 0` in this scene: Platinum's field never uses the specular table, so that part is free here, but it is still wasteful to send 32 uniforms whenever a lighting context that does use it changes
20: - captures at both ends of the window are pixel-identical (`ImageChops.difference` bbox `None` on both screens)
21: 
22: ## Patch (applies to `src/graphics/g3d/g3d.c` as it stands)
23: 
24: ```c
25: /* file scope, next to s_last_pal / s_last_tev */
26: static uint32_t s_last_cull, s_last_depth, s_last_blend;
27: static uint32_t s_last_shininess[32];
28: static bool s_shininess_valid;
29: ```
30: 
31: In `upload_lighting`, replace the shininess loop's guard:
32: 
33: ```c
34: if (light->use_shininess &&
35:     (!s_shininess_valid || memcmp(s_last_shininess, light->shininess,
36:                                   sizeof(s_last_shininess)) != 0)) {
37:     for (unsigned i = 0; i < 32; ++i) {
38:         const uint32_t word = light->shininess[i];
39:         C3D_FVUnifSet(GPU_VERTEX_SHADER, u->shininess + i,
40:                       word & 255u, word >> 8 & 255u, word >> 16 & 255u, word >> 24);
41:     }
42:     memcpy(s_last_shininess, light->shininess, sizeof(s_last_shininess));
43:     s_shininess_valid = true;
44: }
45: ```
46: 
47: In `draw_pass`, culling / depth / blend become compare-then-set, e.g.:
48: 
49: ```c
50: const uint32_t cull = (dbg & KJ_DEBUG_NO_CULL) ? GPU_CULL_NONE
51:                       : faces == 2u                ? GPU_CULL_BACK_CCW
52:                       : faces == 1u                ? GPU_CULL_FRONT_CCW
53:                                                    : GPU_CULL_NONE;
54: if (cull != s_last_cull) {
55:     C3D_CullFace(cull);
56:     s_last_cull = cull;
57: }
58: 
59: const uint32_t depth = ((uint32_t)func << 4) |
60:                        (depth_write ? GPU_WRITE_ALL : GPU_WRITE_COLOR);
61: if (depth != s_last_depth) {
62:     C3D_DepthTest(true, func, depth_write ? GPU_WRITE_ALL : GPU_WRITE_COLOR);
63:     s_last_depth = depth;
64: }
65: /* same shape for the blend mode, keyed on the four factor words */
66: ```
67: 
68: and reset the four caches where `s_draw_program` is invalidated (in `kj_g3d_draw`, next to `s_last_pal = NULL`):
69: 
70: ```c
71: s_last_cull = s_last_depth = s_last_blend = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
72: s_shininess_valid = false;
73: ```
74: 
75: The sentinel is what makes the first batch of a frame unconditional, so a program switch or a new frame never inherits the previous state.
76: 
77: ## One thing that does *not* pay off
78: 
79: I also tried joining contiguous batches with byte-identical state into one `C3D_DrawElements`. In Platinum's field that joins **zero** batches: every batch owns its own matrix palette slice (`palette_slot()` / `KJ_G3_PALETTE`), so adjacency fails on the matrices even when the material matches. Counters from that experiment: `merge joined 0 (blocked state ..., matrices ...)`. Joining would need a union palette plus an index remap, not a memcmp.

1: ## The gap
2: 
3: The engine-side profile answers "how long did `g3d` take", but not "which part of the game asked for it". On sinjoh I spent a day guessing at where the field's 4.3 ms of logic went; two rounds of wrong guesses later, a cheap game-side probe put 2.1 ms of it in one function (`ApplicationManager_Exec` of the field map app) and 236 us in another, in a single run. Without that, every optimization is a guess about which of twenty calls to attack.
4: 
5: This is the facility. It is ~30 lines in the engine and ~10 in the profile print, and it is what produced the attribution table in sinjoh's STATUS (`docs/STATUS.md`, sixth pass).
6: 
7: ## Engine side (`src/runtime/kj_bridge.h`, `src/runtime/kj_frame.c`, `src/graphics/renderer.c`)
8: 
9: ```c
10: /* kj_bridge.h */
11: #define KJ_PROBE_SLOTS 11
12: /* in kj_ds_profile: */
13: uint64_t probe_ticks[KJ_PROBE_SLOTS];
14: uint64_t probe_calls[KJ_PROBE_SLOTS];
15: ```
16: 
17: ```c
18: /* kj_frame.c */
19: static u64 s_probe_ticks[KJ_PROBE_SLOTS];
20: static u32 s_probe_calls[KJ_PROBE_SLOTS];
21: 
22: u64 NitroPort_ProbeNow(void) { return svcGetSystemTick(); }
23: 
24: void NitroPort_NoteProbeSince(unsigned slot, u64 t0)
25: {
26:     if (slot < KJ_PROBE_SLOTS) {
27:         s_probe_ticks[slot] += svcGetSystemTick() - t0;
28:         ++s_probe_calls[slot];
29:     }
30: }
31: /* take_profile: copy + zero both arrays so each window reports its own total */
32: ```
33: 
34: ```c
35: /* renderer.c, the [ds] window line */
36: kj_log("[probe] per game frame: slot 0 %llu us, 1 %llu us, ...", ...);
37: ```
38: 
39: ## Game side (temporary, removed after measuring)
40: 
41: ```c
42: const u64 probeAll = NitroPort_ProbeNow();
43: u64 probeT = probeAll;
44: HandleFieldInput(fieldSystem);
45: NitroPort_NoteProbeSince(1, probeT); probeT = NitroPort_ProbeNow();
46: ...
47: NitroPort_NoteProbeSince(0, probeAll);
48: ```
49: 
50: ## Three things that cost me time, so they are worth encoding
51: 
52: 1. **Use `svcGetSystemTick`, never `OS_GetTick`.** `OS_GetTick` goes through the port's timer emulation, which syncs DS timers: measured at ~8 us per frame for two calls, i.e. the probe becomes a visible fraction of what it measures.
53: 2. **Slots must be siblings, not nested**, or the numbers double-count: slot 0 = the whole call, slots 1..n = its parts. That way "slot 0 minus the sum of the children" is the unattributed remainder, which is the number that tells you where to probe next.
54: 3. **`KJ_PROBE_SLOTS` lives in a shared header, so a partial rebuild can mix slot counts between engine objects.** I hit exactly that: `kj_frame.o` written six slots and `renderer.o` reading eleven, producing a window with missing slots and `0 us` next to a huge draw count. The rule that came out of it is in sinjoh's `docs/LESSONS.md` ("Two builds at once measure a binary that exists in no tree"): after changing the slot count, clean-build, and check object timestamps before believing any probe window.
55: 
56: The probe calls themselves should be compiled out of release (`HGSS_PROFILE_OFF`), since the tick reads are the cost, not the counters.
57: 
58: ## A fourth trap, on the harness side
59: 
60: A window of zeros is not a measurement of "nothing ran". One of my runs printed
61: a complete, internally consistent 600-frame window: `g3d 0 us`,
62: `2D screens skipped 1200`, `3D batches 0`, `g3 Fifo calls 0`, and no `[probe]`
63: line at all. It was a still capture of the journal screen: the harness's third
64: button press had been swallowed, so the game never left the menu. Re-running the
65: same binary on the same harness reached the field and printed the numbers.
66: 
67: If a game-side probe facility gets added, make the harness refuse to record
68: until the game says it is where it thinks it is (a log line, a known screen, a
69: nonzero counter), rather than trusting a fixed button schedule. Sinjoh's
70: `tools/lotus/field_run.py` now presses START until the engine logs its field
71: marker, and still fills the same settle so the windows start on the same
72: pictures.

1: ## The failure mode
2: 
3: A measurement run reported a field split that no source tree could produce: the whole field update 2408 us, its two children absent, three sibling slots `0 us`, all next to 15,520 3D draws. The cause was two builds running against the same object trees at once: the linked binary took `kj_frame.o` from a build that wrote 6 probe slots and `renderer.o` from one that read 11, and they disagree about `kj_ds_profile`'s layout. Nothing failed; the numbers just became fiction.
4: 
5: The same class of bug exists without probes: any edit to a struct in a shared header between two concurrent builds can link a binary whose halves were compiled against different layouts, and it will usually still boot.
6: 
7: ## Proposal: make the build refuse to run twice
8: 
9: A lock file next to the build trees, taken at startup and released at exit, plus a check that the recorded PID is still alive so a crashed build does not block forever:
10: 
11: ```powershell
12: # tools/build.ps1
13: $lock = Join-Path $repo 'build/.build.lock'
14: if (Test-Path $lock) {
15:     $pid = (Get-Content $lock -First 1) -as [int]
16:     if ($pid -and (Get-Process -Id $pid -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
17:         throw "a build is already running (pid $pid); wait for it or remove $lock"
18:     }
19:     Remove-Item $lock   # stale
20: }
21: Set-Content $lock $PID
22: try { ...existing build... } finally { Remove-Item $lock -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
23: ```
24: 
25: Two smaller things that paid for themselves on sinjoh:
26: 
27: - **Print the timestamp of the newest object and of the input header** at the end of the build, or at least of the object that a measurement will depend on. Comparing them is what diagnosed the incident: `kj_frame.o` was older than the header edit while `renderer.o` was newer.
28: - **A `-Clean` flag that removes the per-profile trees but keeps generated SDK headers** is worth having; sinjoh's `-Clean` deletes `nitro/fx/fx_const.h`, which the build does not regenerate, and the next build dies with `fatal error: nitro/fx/fx_const.h: No such file or directory` (regenerate with the SDK's own `gen_fx_const.py`). If kohjoh's `-Clean` has the same hole, fixing it here is cheap.
29: 
30: ## Why this is worth a change rather than a note
31: 
32: The failure is silent and *looks like a result*: the numbers are plausible enough to build a conclusion on. I wrote a day's worth of analysis on top of one before noticing. A lock turns a 4-hour detour into an error message.

1: ## The number worth attacking
2: 
3: On sinjoh's Platinum field (standing, 600-frame windows) the scene submits **26 3D draws per frame for ~568 triangles** ΓÇö about 22 triangles and 20 indices per draw. At the ~9.7 us per separate draw that coffeepot measured on an Old 3DS (`coffeepot/ctr/engineering/PICA200/gpu-rendering.md`, "What a draw call costs"), that is roughly **250 us of CPU per frame** for 26 draws that carry almost no geometry. It is the largest single recoverable block left on the port side of the frame after the state filter in #10.
4: 
5: ## Why the obvious fix does nothing
6: 
7: I implemented "join contiguous batches with identical state into one `C3D_DrawElements`" and measured it: **0 joins in the field** and 0 in the title scene.
8: 
9: ```
10: merge joined 0 (blocked state 15093 matrices 0)
11: ```
12: 
13: The block is the *material*, not the matrix palette: every consecutive batch differs in `poly_attr`/`tex_param`/`tex_pltt`. A DS batch is a material with its own palette slice, not a strip of one material ΓÇö that is the structural reason the draw count is high.
14: 
15: ## What would actually cut it
16: 
17: Two changes together, in this order:
18: 
19: 1. **A union palette per draw.** A batch's matrices are a slice of the frame's matrix array (`first_matrix`/`matrix_count`, `KJ_G3_PALETTE` slots). Several batches that share a state but not a matrix set could share one draw if the vertex shader were given the union of their matrices and their indices were remapped to the union's slots. That needs a per-frame rewritten index buffer (or a per-batch palette index patch), not a `memcmp`.
20: 
21: 2. **Grouping by state, not by storage order.** Once the palette is a union, batches become joinable only if they are *sorted* by material. For the opaque pass with depth testing that is safe (the DS's own order only matters for equal-depth ties and for translucent geometry, which stays in its own pass). Translucent batches must keep their order.
22: 
23: The rewrite cost is small against the win: 26 draws ├ù ~9.7 us Γëê 250 us saved, against rewriting ~1700 indices per frame (a few microseconds) plus one palette upload per joined group.
24: 
25: ## What I can and cannot claim
26: 
27: - **Claimed (measured):** 26 draws/frame, ~22 triangles per draw, zero adjacency joins with byte-identical state, 38,511 of 46,680 `C3D_*` setter calls redundant (the #10 fix).
28: - **Not measured:** the union-palette join. I have not implemented it; the 250 us figure is arithmetic from the per-draw cost coffeepot measured, not a sinjoh measurement.
29: 
30: If anyone wants the counters that answered the adjacency question, they are three `uint32_t`s in `kj_g3d_stats` and a `[gpu]` print ΓÇö worth adding before starting, so the join count and the decline reason show up in the same window as the timing.

1: # Running kohjoh in LOTUS
2: 
3: LOTUS is a second integration debugger beside Azahar. It runs the same
4: Azahar-derived core as `tools/azahar/run.ps1` but drives it from a native worker
5: process over a local MCP server, so frames are advanced deterministically
6: instead of being screenshotted at wall-clock times. It is **not** an O3DS timing
7: authority either: every result from it is EMULATOR-only evidence
8: ([kohjoh.md 1](../kohjoh.md)).
9: 
10: Installed at `C:\Users\terezi\workdir\LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64` (portable ZIP,
11: v0.0.1). Its own documentation is in that folder's `docs/`; the relevant pages
12: are `20`-`26`, especially `21-native-control.md` (worker protocol) and
13: `23-local-mcp.md` (the stdio MCP surface).
14: 
15: ## Fixed configuration
16: 
17: The native worker runs Old 3DS, software rendering, HLE services, HLE/muted DSP,
18: guest ticks 0 and guest time 2000-01-01 UTC, with no window. Nothing here is
19: configurable through MCP; the host JSON is trusted startup input that the model
20: cannot change.
21: 
22: ## Backend
23: 
24: Both backends run kohjoh. They are the same Azahar core at the same pin
25: (`05773bbb5`); the only build difference is `-DCTR_BACKEND_NAME`, which changes
26: the reported `backend_name` and nothing else. `LOTUS.cmd`/`CITnLO` is the
27: default; `LOTUS-AZAHAR.cmd`/`--backend AZAHAR` is the upstream-tracking one.
28: 
29: Two things look like failures and are not:
30: 
31: - **`Failed to find title id for ROM (Error 0)`** is logged by *every* `.3dsx`
32:   load, including sessions that then run for thousands of frames, so it is not a
33:   usable failure signal. kohjoh's `.3dsx` has no SMDH (`header_size = 0x20`, no
34:   `SMDH` magic, because `make_smdh` finds no icon), which is what the
35:   `SelfNCCH ... might be a 3dsx file` warning refers to; neither backend needs
36:   the banner. The Homebrew Launcher on real hardware does not either.
37: - **A session that ends with an 8-line worker log and an empty `sdmc/`** was
38:   usually created and then abandoned: sessions die with the MCP server, and
39:   `lotus_create_session` has by then loaded and paused the guest, so closing the
40:   server immediately leaves no guest log at all. Confirm with
41:   `lotus_session_status` before concluding the load failed.
42: 
43: ## Sessions and the private SD card
44: 
45: Each session is its own worker process with its own root:
46: 
47: ```text
48: <lotus>/data/<profile>/sessions/<handle>/
49:   sdmc/            # guest SD card: sdmc:/ maps here
50:   nand/  sysdata/  log/  cheats/
51: ```
52: 
53: `lotus_create_session` loads the approved asset **immediately** and pauses, so
54: kohjoh starts before its data pack exists unless the pack is already there. The
55: sequence is therefore:
56: 
57: 1. create the session (kohjoh boots, reports no pack, idles),
58: 2. copy the pack, manifest, save and input script into that session's `sdmc`,
59: 3. `reset` — the worker reloads the same content with the new SD contents.
60: 
61: Sessions belong to the MCP server process that created them and cannot be
62: re-attached later: closing the server (or OpenCode restarting it) ends them, and
63: each new session needs its own staged copy of the pack (125 MB, a few seconds on
64: local disk).
65: 
66: Guest paths kohjoh uses:
67: 
68: ```text
69: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/data/<edition>.pak
70: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/data/<edition>.manifest.json
71: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/saves/<edition>.sav
72: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/script.txt
73: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/logs/<edition>.log
74: sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/dumps/
75: ```
76: 
77: ## Harness: `tools/lotus/run.py`
78: 
79: The equivalent of `tools/azahar/run.ps1` for LOTUS. It creates a session,
80: stages the requested files, resets, advances frames in chunks, presses buttons
81: and writes PNG captures plus the guest log location.
82: 
83: ```sh
84: python tools/lotus/run.py --pack build/prepare-test/heartgold.pak \
85:   --manifest build/prepare-test/heartgold.manifest.json \
86:   --artifact build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx \
87:   --frames 3000 --shots 1200,1800,2400,3000 --tag boot
88: 
89: python tools/lotus/run.py --artifact build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx \
90:   --pack build/prepare-test/heartgold.pak --manifest build/prepare-test/heartgold.manifest.json \
91:   --frames 1200 --press 600:START --shots 1200 --tag title
92: ```
93: 
94: | Option | Effect |
95: | --- | --- |
96: | `--artifact` | `.3dsx` to run (default `build/kj/pokeheartgold.3dsx`) |
97: | `--edition` | `heartgold` (default) or `soulsilver`, selects the SD file names |
98: | `--pack`, `--manifest` | stage the data pack into this session's SD card |
99: | `--save path` / `--fresh-save` | install a save / delete the session's save |
100: | `--script file` | scripted input (`tests/inputs/*.txt`); absent, none is staged |
101: | `--frames`, `--chunk` | total frames, and frames per native request (default 60) |
102: | `--shots 10,30` | capture at those frame numbers (the last frame always captured) |
103: | `--press FRAME:KEYS` | hold keys over a frame boundary, e.g. `900:DOWN+A`, `600:START` |
104: | `--touch FRAME:X,Y` | touch the bottom screen at native `320x240` coordinates, e.g. `5000:160,120` |
105: | `--hold` | pause before each capture |
106: | `--backend`, `--lotus` | `AZAHAR` (default) or `CITnLO`; LOTUS install root |
107: | `--tag`, `--out-dir` | output folder: `build/lotus/<tag>/` |
108: 
109: Captures are written as `f<frame>-top.png` (400x240) and `f<frame>-bottom.png`
110: (320x240), converted from the worker's normalized BGRA8 output. Each capture's
111: SHA-256 is printed, so pictures can be compared with Azahar or melonDS runs.
112: 
113: ## MCP from OpenCode
114: 
115: `C:\Users\terezi\workdir\opencode.json` registers the server, so this session and
116: any future one get the `lotus_*` tools:
117: 
118: ```json
119: {
120:   "mcp": {
121:     "servers": {
122:       "lotus": {
123:         "type": "local",
124:         "command": [
125:           "C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64\\bin\\lotus-mcp.exe",
126:           "C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\LOTUS-v0.0.1-windows-x64\\data\\azahar\\host.json"
127:         ]
128:       }
129:     }
130:   }
131: }
132: ```
133: 
134: Re-register with `opencode mcp add lotus -- <lotus-mcp.exe> <host.json>` and
135: check with `opencode mcp list`. The host JSON at the path above is the server's
136: whole configuration:
137: 
138: ```json
139: {
140:   "worker": ".../runtimes/azahar/ctr-worker.exe",
141:   "storage_root": ".../data/azahar/sessions",
142:   "assets": {"homebrew": ".../build/kj-gold-normal/pokeheartgold.3dsx"},
143:   "allow_control": true
144: }
145: ```
146: 
147: `launch.ps1 -Backend AZAHAR -Mode MCP -Fixture <3dsx>` rewrites it with absolute
148: paths, which is the supported way to point the server at a different artifact
149: (do not run it with `-Mode MCP` while the server is connected: it starts a
150: second, competing stdio server).
151: 
152: | Tool | Use |
153: | --- | --- |
154: | `lotus_status` | protocol, owned sessions, approved asset handles |
155: | `lotus_create_session` | load `homebrew` (the only asset) into a new private session |
156: | `lotus_run_until` | advance 1-600 frames, 20 host-second deadline |
157: | `lotus_control` | `pause`, `reset`, `stop` |
158: | `lotus_input` | complete buttons/touch state; owner `live` |
159: | `lotus_capture` | two `lotus://artifact/...` resource links (BGRA8) |

163: An agent driving kohjoh by hand:

166: 2. Copy the pack and manifest into
167:    `data/azahar/sessions/<handle>/sdmc/3ds/kohjoh/data/`.
168: 3. `lotus_control {"session": ..., "operation": "reset"}`.
169: 4. `lotus_run_until` in chunks of ~60 frames; read `frames` from the reply.
170: 5. `lotus_capture`, then read each URI from `resources/read` (base64 blob).
171: 
172: The worker enforces four sessions, 600 frames and a 20 host-second deadline per
173: call, and 128 retained captures; a call that hits the deadline still reports the
174: frames it reached (`last_error: host_deadline`), so retry from that number.

176: ## Limits and what LOTUS cannot show
177: 
178: - **Speed**: the software renderer runs far slower than real time for kohjoh's
179:   3D scenes; a 60-frame request can hit its 20-second deadline mid-intro. Do not

189:   frame 0 instead.

191:   reproducible but not a real console's RTC.

# Build on Windows

Verified 2026-11-12 on Windows 11 with a **from-scratch** bootstrap and build
(empty `build/upstream`, empty `build/kj`): 91 patches applied, 0 errors,
`.3dsx` packaged in about 6 minutes, and the title screen checked in Azahar.
Output: a HeartGold `.3dsx`. SoulSilver and CIA are not built yet.

## Requirements

| Tool | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| devkitPro | `C:\devkitPro` | Packages: devkitARM, libctru, citro3d, 3dstools, picasso. Versions are pinned in [`upstream.lock`](../upstream.lock). Its MSYS2 (`C:\devkitPro\msys2`) supplies `bash`, `make` and Python 3.14 (`/usr/bin/python`). |
| Git for Windows | `C:\Program Files\Git` | **Required for bootstrap.** devkitPro MSYS2's own `git` cannot fetch over HTTPS (see [pitfalls](#pitfalls)). |
| Azahar | `C:\Program Files\Azahar\azahar.exe` | Testing only (`tools/azahar/run.ps1`). |
| PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) | | Runs the Azahar harness. |
| ROM | your own verified US dump | Only needed for the data pack. Never commit ROMs, packs, saves or extracted data. |

## Build

Run every build step **inside devkitPro's MSYS2 login shell**
(`C:\devkitPro\msys2\usr\bin\bash.exe -lc "..."`). The login profile
(`/etc/profile.d/devkit-env.sh`) sets `DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro` and
`DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM`, which the build reads to find
`arm-none-eabi-gcc`. Use absolute `/c/...` paths throughout.

From Git Bash or PowerShell:

```sh
C:/devkitPro/msys2/usr/bin/bash.exe -lc '
  export PATH="/c/Program Files/Git/cmd:$PATH"    # Git for Windows first (HTTPS)
  K=/c/Users/<you>/workdir/kohjoh
  cd $K
  python tools/game/bootstrap.py                   # pinned decomp + every patch in patches/
  python tools/game/check_patches.py               # fails if build/upstream lacks a patch
  python tools/game/hgss_game.py --root $K/build/upstream --target 3ds --out $K/build/kj -j 32
' > build/kj-build.log 2>&1
```

**`--target 3ds` is required.** The default is `host32`, a PC build for tests.

A build succeeded only if the log ends with
`packaged .../pokeheartgold.3dsx` **and** has no `error:` lines. If the
vendored SDK/NitroSystem library fails to compile, the build prints
`warning: the vendored library build failed; linking with libnitrosystem.a,
libnitro.a ...` and **still packages a `.3dsx` from stale libraries**. Any
SDK or NitroSystem change is then silently absent. Check for it:

```sh
grep -E "error:|vendored library build failed" build/kj-build.log   # must print nothing
```

### Outputs (`--out build/kj`)

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `pokeheartgold.3dsx` | the program |
| `pokeheartgold-3ds.elf` | symbols, linked at 0x00100000 (`arm-none-eabi-addr2line -e` for crash addresses) |
| `pokeheartgold.build-info.txt` | commit, dirty flag, sha256, the state of every legacy flag |
| `obj/`, `app/`, `ctr/`, `sdk/`, `gen/` | incremental objects and generated headers |
| `link.log`, `link-<utc>.log` | linker output; unresolved symbols are reported here |

The shared vendored-library trees are `build/hgss-sdk`, `build/hgss-nns`, and
`build/NitroSDK` / `build/NitroSystem` (links into `build/upstream/lib`).

### Timing and incremental builds

- Bootstrap ≈ 1 min (shallow fetch + `git am` of the patch stack).
- First build ≈ 5 min at `-j 32`. A rebuild after a kohjoh-side change takes
  about 2 min. Game objects are skipped when they are newer than their source
  and every `-MMD` dependency and their flags match; the Nitro libraries are
  re-made by `make`.
- Build each variant into its own `--out` (e.g. `--out $K/build/kjz
  --define KJ_G3_ZERO_TRACE`) so variants never mix objects.

"""Run the kohjoh LOTUS session to chosen frames, capturing PNGs at each.

Usage: python tools/lotus/shots.py <session> <outdir> <frame> [<frame>...]

Frames must be increasing. Each target is reached by 600-frame chunks whose
progress is re-read from the session status after every chunk (a chunk may
stop early at the host deadline). Captures are written as
<outdir>/f<NNNNN>-top.png and f<NNNNN>-bottom.png.
"""
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

CTL = "sinjoh/tools/lotus/ctl.py"
CWD = r"C:\Users\terezi\workdir"


def call(name, args, timeout=900):
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, CTL, "call", name, json.dumps(args)],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=CWD, timeout=timeout)
    text = out.stdout + out.stderr
    try:
        return json.loads(text[text.find("{"):])
    except (ValueError, IndexError):
        raise SystemExit(f"ctl {name} failed: {text[:400]}")


def session_frames(session):
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, CTL, "status"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=CWD)
    d = json.loads(out.stdout[out.stdout.find("{"):])
    for s in d["sessions"]:
        if s["id"].startswith(session[:8]):
            return s["telemetry"]["frames"]
    raise SystemExit(f"session {session} not found")


def main():
    session, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    targets = [int(x) for x in sys.argv[3:]]
    if targets != sorted(set(targets)):
        raise SystemExit("targets must be increasing and unique")
    for target in targets:
        done = session_frames(session)
        while done < target:
            r = call("lotus_run_until", {"session": session, "frames": min(600, target - done)})
            if r.get("last_error"):
                print("last_error:", r["last_error"], flush=True)
            done = session_frames(session)
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, CTL, "capture", session, "--out", outdir],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=CWD)
        if "saved:" not in out.stdout and not out.stderr:
            raise SystemExit(out.stdout + out.stderr)
        top = out.stdout.split("saved:")[1].strip().split(", ")[0]
        base, _ = top.rsplit("-", 1)
        shutil.move(top, f"{outdir}/f{done:05d}-top.png")
        shutil.move(base + "-bottom.png", f"{outdir}/f{done:05d}-bottom.png")
        print(f"f{done:05d} captured", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

 # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- main
 
+def build_lock(out: Path):
+    """Refuse to run two builds against one --out tree (issue #12).
+
+    Two concurrent builds mix object layouts (a shared header change
+    compiles some objects with the old struct, some with the new) and link
+    a binary whose halves disagree; it usually still boots, so the only
+    symptom is measurement fiction. The lock is per --out tree; a stale
+    file whose PID is gone is removed."""
+    import atexit
+
+    lock = out / ".build.lock"
+    if lock.is_file():
+        try:
+            pid = int(lock.read_text().strip() or 0)
+        except ValueError:
+            pid = 0
+        if pid and pid != os.getpid():
+            alive = False
+            try:
+                os.kill(pid, 0)
+                alive = True
+            except OSError:
+                pass
+            if alive:
+                raise SystemExit(
+                    f"hgss_game: a build is already running on {out} "
+                    f"(pid {pid}); wait for it or remove {lock}")
+        print(f"hgss_game: removing a stale build lock (pid {pid})", file=sys.stderr)
+    lock.write_text(str(os.getpid()))
+
+    def release():
+        try:
+            if lock.read_text().strip() == str(os.getpid()):
+                lock.unlink()
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+
+    atexit.register(release)
+    return release
+
+
+def print_freshness_stamp(out: Path) -> None:
+    """Print the newest object and the newest port header (issue #12).
+
+    Comparing these two timestamps is what diagnosed the mixed-layout
+    incident: kj_frame.o was older than the header edit while renderer.o
+    was newer, and the numbers were fiction. A measurement that depends on
+    a struct layout should check this line before believing a window."""
+    try:
+        objects = sorted(out.rglob("*.o"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
+        headers = sorted((REPO / "src").rglob("*.h"), key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
+        if objects and headers:
+            fmt = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
+            o, h = objects[-1], headers[-1]
+            print(f"   [fresh] newest object {o.relative_to(out)} "
+                  f"({datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(o.stat().st_mtime, datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(fmt)} UTC), "
+                  f"newest header {h.relative_to(REPO)} "
+                  f"({datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(h.stat().st_mtime, datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(fmt)} UTC)")
+    except OSError:

"""Byte-compare a LOTUS capture folder's PNGs against reference PNGs.

Usage: python tools/lotus/compare.py <new_dir> <ref_dir>
Compares files whose names match fNNNNN-top.png / fNNNNN-bottom.png present
in both folders; prints sha256 and PASS/DIFF per file.
"""
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def sha(p: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]


def main() -> int:
    new, ref = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
    failures = 0
    for f in sorted(new.glob("f*-*.png")):
        g = ref / f.name
        if not g.is_file():
            print(f"{f.name}: no reference")
            continue
        same = sha(f) == sha(g)
        print(f"{f.name}: {'PASS' if same else 'DIFF'} ({sha(f)} vs {sha(g)})")
        failures += 0 if same else 1
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

All test traffic then goes through the bridge:

```sh
python tools/lotus/ctl.py status
python tools/lotus/ctl.py create --kind primary --card sinjoh --asset sinjoh
python tools/lotus/ctl.py run <session> 600        # <=600-frame batches
python tools/lotus/ctl.py capture <session> --out build/lotus/cap
python tools/lotus/ctl.py sessions
python tools/lotus/ctl.py stop <session>
python tools/lotus/ctl.py call lotus_session_status '{"session":"<session>"}'
```

A session handle belongs to the bridge's supervisor, not to the client that
created it: any `ctl.py` connection can run, capture or stop it, and it stays
listed to everyone. Create sessions for a test and `stop` them when done; a
`secondary` is deleted on stop, a `primary` keeps its card. The bridge
serialises MCP calls (one worker call at a time), so parallel sessions advance
by turns rather than truly simultaneously; that is the intended shared mode.
`max_sessions` is 4 in `shared-host.json`.

Use different cards per project and per scratch run: `sinjoh`, `kohjoh`, and
throw-away secondaries. A card's guest SD is
`<lotus>/data/citnlo/sessions/cards/<card>/sdmc/`; sinjoh's `stage_card.py`
fills the `sinjoh` card with `3ds/sinjoh-platinum*.3dsx` and `3ds/sinjoh/`,
and kohjoh copies its own files into its card from its pack. The two projects
also use different guest paths (`sdmc:/3ds/sinjoh` and `sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh`), so
a card from one cannot feed the other.

If the bridge exits, its sessions stop (a primary card keeps its data). Keep
the bridge process alive for the whole working session; `ctl.py shutdown`
closes it cleanly.

`tools/lotus/run_sinjoh.py` remains for a self-contained run that opens and
closes its own window; use the bridge when tests should share the window.

## Windowed, over MCP

`lotus-desktop.exe --mcp <host.json>` opens the window and serves the same MCP
tools on stdin/stdout, so the person watches the session the harness drives.
`lotus-mcp.exe <config>` is the headless variant. A session handle expires when
the server process exits; a primary card keeps its `sdmc/` data.

`sinjoh-host.json` in the LOTUS folder is the one-shot config (the bridge uses
`shared-host.json`); both approve the builds and prefer Vulkan:

```json
{
  "worker": "<lotus>/runtimes/citnlo/ctr-worker.exe",
  "storage_root": "<lotus>/data/citnlo/sessions",
  "assets": {
    "sinjoh": "<repo>/build/game/3ds/sinjoh-platinum.3dsx",
    "sinjoh-dbg": "<repo>/build/game/3ds-prof/sinjoh-platinum-dbg.3dsx"
  },
  "asset_directories": {
    "release": "<repo>/build/game/3ds",
    "debug": "<repo>/build/game/3ds-prof"
  },
  "allow_control": true,
  "prefer_vulkan": true,
  "max_sessions": 4
}
```

`prefer_vulkan` is the default; a refusal at load is reported as
`renderer_fallback`. The session status reports `renderer: "vulkan"` and an
empty fallback when it is the real thing. `graphics_api: 0` in a profile pins
software for a reference run.

## Driving it

```sh
# Stage the programs, pack, manifest and save into a persistent card, and
# optionally a script.txt for deterministic input.
python tools/lotus/stage_card.py --card sinjoh --script tests/inputs/lotus_field.txt

# Open the window, create a primary session on that card, run N frames,
# capture both screens as PNG and stop.
python tools/lotus/run_sinjoh.py --asset sinjoh --card sinjoh --frames 900
python tools/lotus/run_sinjoh.py --asset sinjoh-dbg --frames 600 --keep
```

`--hold SECONDS` leaves the window open after the capture; `--keep` also leaves
the session running until the client exits. The process owns the session, so
the run ends when the client does.

For a repeatable steady state, `tools/lotus/field_run.py` drives the title into
the field and records whole 600-picture windows from the standing field:

```sh
python tools/lotus/field_run.py --asset sinjoh-dbg --windows 2 --out build/lotus/field_now
```

It creates the session, runs the title (6600 frames), presses START, A
(Continue), START, then records each window and saves `top.png`/`bottom.png` for
the last one. The second START is the journal's: it turns pages on A/left/right
and closes on START or B at page 0 (`journal_controller.c`), so a one-page save
looks frozen if you keep pressing A. Windows land on the same picture numbers
every run, which is what makes two builds comparable: capture the same picture
in both, diff with `ImageChops`, and expect `bbox None`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the four shipping variants, one at a time, and print their .3dsx paths.

Usage (inside the devkitPro MSYS2 login shell, after tools/bootstrap.py):

    python tools/game/build_variants.py                # gold/silver x normal/prof
    python tools/game/build_variants.py --only gold-prof
    python tools/game/build_variants.py --list
    python tools/game/build_variants.py --jobs 16

Each variant gets its own --out (build/kj-<variant>): the game objects differ
between editions and between HGSS_PROFILE=on (prof) and unset (normal). The
variants run strictly sequentially. They share the SDK/NitroSystem shim
(build/hgss-sdk, build/hgss-nns) and the headers generated under
build/upstream, so parallel variants race on both; the lost race is
`mklink /J ... Cannot create a file when that file already exists`.

A variant counts as built only when hgss_game.py exits 0, its .3dsx exists, and
its log has no `error:` or `vendored library build failed` line (see
docs/building-windows.md). The first failure stops the run and prints the log
path; a full run ends with the four paths.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
TOOLS = REPO / "tools" / "game"
DEFAULT_ROOT = REPO / "build" / "upstream"

sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS))
import hgss_nitro as nitro  # noqa: E402 (msys(): the /c/... spelling make needs)

# (variant, --game, HGSS_PROFILE). "normal" is the uninstrumented build.
VARIANTS = (
    ("gold-normal", "heartgold", False),
    ("gold-prof", "heartgold", True),
    ("silver-normal", "soulsilver", False),
    ("silver-prof", "soulsilver", True),
)

# A build that compiled nothing new but linked, or fell back to stale
# libraries, still exits 0 and still packages a .3dsx. docs/building-windows.md
# says to grep for these two markers.
BAD_MARKERS = ("error:", "vendored library build failed")


def output_dir(variant: str) -> Path:
    return REPO / "build" / f"kj-{variant}"


def log_path(variant: str) -> Path:
    return REPO / "build" / f"kj-{variant}-build.log"

# AGENTS.md

Repository-wide rules for agent sessions working on kohjoh.

## READ THE WIKI 

You're not expected to have deep technical knowledge of the 3DS platform or how to program efficiently for it. This information has been collected for you already. If it isn't already on disk, clone https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot.git. Always refer to coffeepot's CTR section when you're writing code or planning project changes - read the relevant hardware, firrmware or engineering articles, so you understand what you're working with. If you can't justify a change with real-hardware evidence or a citation from the wiki, you probably should not do it. Never edit coffeepot yourself. If you notice something genuinely incorrect, PR and tell the user. Always follow the wiki's C style guide.

The coffeepot wiki is provided locally on this machine in workdir/coffeepot/.
## Delegating to subagents

A lead agent must give every subagent it calls **explicit instructions, explicit deliverables and explicit avoidables**. This is not optional, and it matters most for implementer agents: they edit files and cannot rely on chat context the lead has not written down.

Every subagent brief must state, in the prompt itself:

1. **Objective** — the one bounded slice to complete, and why it exists.
2. **Allowed paths** — the exact files or directories the subagent may read and edit.
3. **Deliverables** — the concrete output: code, patch files, tests, docs, and the required report format (files changed, commands run, results, open questions).
4. **Acceptance checks** — the commands or observations that prove the work is done, and the expected result.
5. **Avoidables** — what not to touch or do: paths outside the slice, unrelated refactors, the decomp checkout in place, commits/pushes unless explicitly assigned, and any known traps from `kohjoh.md` or `docs/troubleshooting.md`.
6. **Stopping point** — when to stop and report instead of guessing, for example if the slice grows, the brief conflicts with `kohjoh.md`, or an acceptance check cannot pass.

Do not send a subagent a vague goal and let it infer scope. If the lead cannot fill in all six items, the slice is not ready to delegate. A brief that is broader, vaguer or in conflict with `kohjoh.md` should be revised before the call, not discovered by the subagent mid-edit.

Implementer subagents hold `docs/status.md`, `docs/lessons.md` and `kohjoh.md` as required reading; the brief adds the slice-specific detail those files cannot contain. When this file disagrees with an agent definition under `.opencode/agents/` or `.claude/agents/`, this file wins.

## Git identity

The only git identity an agent may use in this repository is:

```text
terezi <jules@foxtails.me>
```

Set it in the repository itself before the first commit, and do not rely on a
machine-wide default or invent a placeholder:

```sh
git config user.name terezi
git config user.email jules@foxtails.me
```

Every agent commit carries both fields. Do not use `A4`,
`a4@example.invalid`, the host's auto-detected address, or any other
identity, and do not author on someone else's behalf. If a commit already
exists under another identity, report it to the lead rather than rewriting
history: an artifact's `build-info` names the commit it was built from, and
re-authoring a commit changes that name.
